parsedVerdict.reasoning:
RegistrationsService is an application-layer use-case service, and what it contains fits that role. It loads aggregates through repository interfaces declared in the domain layer and hands the business decision to the domain: RegistrationPolicy.assertCanRegister, workshop.takeSeat/releaseSeat and registration.cancel. It then saves the results and maps them to application DTOs.

Every parameter and return type is declared by the project itself: RegisterAttendeeDto, RegistrationResponseDto, WorkshopResponseDto and string ids. None of them come from a web, transport or framework package. There are no HTTP request, response, status-code or HTTP-exception types.

The only framework items are the NestJS @Injectable/@Inject decorators. Under the rubric, decorators are banned only in domain files, so they are allowed in an application service.

Errors are raised with the project's own DomainError, not an HTTP exception. The service does no direct persistence or I/O; it only calls repository abstractions.

The clone flags point to duplicated code shared with WorkshopsService.findOne. That is a duplication issue, not a code-in-the-wrong-layer issue, so it is out of scope for this rule.
